chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: Opening at the Cotton Club as house band for six months
summary: Crawford describes the Cotton Club as the top New York club, the band's second job, replacing Cab Calloway as house band for about six months.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So now what was the -- what was the -- now, you told me you had to play like vaudeville -- vaudeville show when you were at the Lafayette -- so the first job you had in New York was Lafayette, right?
That's what it was, vaudeville, with a chorus line.
So it was a vaudeville house, with a chorus line. And so now, you played for the comedians and the dancers and the chorus line and then you played -- then you played like a music part?
Yeah, we did (inaudible). our number
Then you all did your number?
Yeah, whatever we did, flashy.
Then the next job was with the Cotton Club.
Yeah.
What was that like?
Oh, that was -- Cotton Club? That was Utopia. That was cream of the crop.
This is 1933.
Yeah, around in there. Cotton Club was the biggest and most popular club in New York City, not just speaking of Harlem. Now, I told you only --
Now, how many people did it hold, about?
That I can't tell you, but the Cotton Club must have held -- George Raft and all the movie stars used to come in there. I can't tell you.
Do you think it held 300 people?
Oh, yeah, tables and dance floor, any act, anybody that go in the Cotton Club, they supposed to have been somebody.
You all -- this was you all's second job after coming to New York.
Yeah.
So you -- so you left the Lafayette and then you went into the Cotton Club?
Yeah.
And how long did you all work at the Cotton Club the first time?
About
Six months.
Oh, you went in for a long stay?
Yeah, we went in like the house band.
Was that when -- was Duke Ellington in Europe at the time?
I'm pretty sure he was, maybe so.
Because I think he went to England.
We went in behind Cab Calloway, because I remember -- yes, that's what we did. That's why I bought -- had to buy all those my own drums.
